message.reasoning_content:
The watch is an Audemars Piguet Royal Oak, stainless steel, blue "Grande Tapisserie" dial, with date at 3 o'clock. Likely reference 15500ST.OO.1220ST.01 (41mm, blue dial) — but the date window position and dial... The 15500ST has date at 3, blue dial ref 15500ST.OO.1220ST.01. The newer 16202ST has blue dial too (50th anniversary). The 15510ST replaced 15500 with date at 3 and blue dial 15510ST.OO.1220ST.01.

Looking at the dial: rectangular hour markers, "AUDEMARS PIGUET" logo with applied AP logo above. Date at 3 o'clock. The minute track... The 15500 has no "AP" applied logo above the brand name? Actually 15500 has applied AP monogram at 12 and "AUDEMARS PIGUET" printed. The 16202 has the "AUDEMARS PIGUET" printed with AP logo applied? Hmm.

In photo, there's a small applied AP logo at 12 and "AUDEMARS PIGUET" text below it. That matches 15500/15510/16202 family. Blue dial with Grande Tapisserie.

Given dial blue with date at 3 and applied AP logo, 15500ST.OO.1220ST.01 is the classic answer. The 15510ST.OO.1220ST.01 also.

I'll guess 15500ST.OO.1220ST.01 with moderate confidence.

Actually, look carefully: the date window at 3 o'clock appears to be a white date on... The 15500 has date at 3:15-ish? No, 15500 has date at 3. The 15400 also. The markers on this watch — the hour markers seem thin and short, look at 12 o'clock: two batons. Hmm.

Case appears slightly slimmer; hard to tell. I'll go with 15500ST.OO.1220ST.01, confidence ~0.45.
